summary.headline: Kissht Q1 FY27: PAT rose 59% YoY to INR 95 crore and AUM 61% YoY to INR 8,001 crore, with credit cost down to 6.80% of average AUM.
summary.overview: Management reported AUM of INR 8,001 crore (+61% YoY, +13% QoQ) and PAT of INR 95 crore (+59% YoY, +16% QoQ), with ROAA at 5.05% and ROAE at 21.20%. Credit cost fell to 6.80% of average AUM from 7.02% in Q4 FY26 and 8.85% in Q1 FY26. Total income as a share of average AUM fell 249 bps QoQ, which management attributed to deliberate pricing for higher-quality customers and a rise in off-book share from 49.7% to 53.6%. Management reiterated FY27 guidance (AUM growth of 40%+, 15% credit cost reduction, ROA of 5%+ and ROE of 20%+) and said it is on track.

segments.name: Personal loans (PL)
segments.commentary: Customer rate about 29-30%; including processing fees, bounce and penal charges, and insurance income, effective yield about 36-37%. Management said PL is the core growth engine.

segments.name: Loan against property (LAP)
segments.commentary: AUM INR 617 crore, 7.7% of total. Yield ranges from 16% to 23-24%, average about 21.8%. Management expects breakeven around Q3 FY27 and targets 20%+ ROE. Branch breakeven reportedly takes 7-8 months versus 16-18 months for an average branch, helped by about 40% of LAP customers coming from the PL base.

segments.name: Mutual fund distribution (new)
segments.commentary: Subsidiary has received AMFI registration. Management described this as a fee-income line; no size or timing was given.

guidance_outlook: AUM growth guided at 40%+ over the next 12 months; management said it expects to over-deliver, given 13% QoQ growth in Q1.
Credit cost to fall about 15% in FY27 (from the 8.85% Q1 FY26 level); management said it is tracking well.
Cost of borrowing to fall at least 100 bps over the next three quarters, mainly in H2 FY27; over three years management sees 200-300 bps.
Opex benefit: management expects operating leverage to add about 4-5% to returns over three years.
Management committed to ROA of 5%+ and ROE of 20%+ consistently. It described a three-year plan to pass through about 8-9% of revenue margin while holding ROA.
Possible credit rating upgrades from India Ratings and CRISIL under discussion; management said any upgrade would affect FY28 borrowing costs more than FY27.
capex_capacity: LAP scaled to 101 branches in eight states; management said it adds branches almost every quarter.
Capital raised through the May 2026 IPO of about INR 850 crore; NBFC capital adequacy rose to 40.2%.

Technology: underwriting uses 7,200+ signals; AUC of the model is 74% (66% in 2023); more than 7,000 field agents and 1,000+ tele-callers; over 95% of collections handled in-house; more than 80% of own code written with AI.
demand_pricing: Management attributed the fall in revenue margin to the higher share of lower-priced repeat, high-quality customers and the rise in off-book share, which earns a servicing fee instead of interest income.
Organic channel share of sourcing rose to 31% in Q1 from 27% in Q4 and about 23-24% average in FY26; management aims for 40-50% over time.
Paused lending in about 450 pin codes in Q4 FY26; reopened 180 (about 40%) in Q1 and kept 270 paused. Business is in about 11,000 of 17,000 pin codes, which contribute 98% of business.

Tightened underwriting for salaried applicants without recent EPFO credits and for self-employed borrowers with weaker banking credit. Approval band was moved to 3.7 from 4 in specific segments; management is reviewing this.
Management said bureau data shows stress in small-ticket loans and multi-lender borrowers at industry level, but its own post-December 2025 vintages are performing better.
Management said July collections improved versus June, and that Q1 seasonality in bounce rates should reverse in July-September.

qa_highlights.question: What drove AUM growth this quarter and is it sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management credited model-driven approvals of a high share of good-quality customers, plus reopening some previously paused pin codes; it said the growth is sustainable for the foreseeable future.

qa_highlights.question: Can AUM growth exceed the 40%+ guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Ranvir Singh said 13% QoQ growth already in Q1 means the company expects to over-deliver on the 40%+ 12-month AUM growth guidance.

qa_highlights.question: Pin-code pause status: how many were paused now versus last quarter, and how does this square with higher bounce and slightly lower collection efficiency?
qa_highlights.answer: Of about 11,000 pin codes contributing 98% of business (out of 17,000 served), 450 were paused in Q4 FY26; 180 were reopened and 270 remain paused. Management cited credit cost falling to 6.80% from 7.02% and said Q1 bounce seasonality should reverse in July-September, with July collections better than June.

qa_highlights.question: Yield and cost of funds: PL vs LAP yield, incremental cost of funds, and margin outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: PL customer rate 29-30%, effective yield 36-37% including fees; LAP yield 16% to 23-24%, average about 21.8%. One Q1 raise carried a loaded cost of about 12.9%, about 150 bps below FY26 average borrowing cost; reported 4.45% AUM-level cost moved to daily-average basis (about 10 bps better). Cost of borrowing expected to fall at least 100 bps over three quarters, mainly H2 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Share of organic sourcing and medium-term yield/ROA bridge?
qa_highlights.answer: Organic channel share rose to 31% in Q1 from 27% in Q4 and about 23-24% average in FY26, with a target of 40-50%. Over three years management sees about 4-5% benefit from operating leverage, 200-300 bps from lower cost of funds, and risk reduction, totalling about 8-9% of revenue margin passed through while holding ROA at 5%+.

qa_highlights.question: What is the industry stress signal and how has underwriting changed for specific profiles?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said industry bureau data shows stress in recent sourcing; its own post-December 2025 sourcing is performing better. It tightened salaried applicants lacking recent EPFO credits (now using account aggregator data) and self-employed borrowers with weaker banking credit, and approval band was moved to 3.7 from 4 in specific segments, now under review.

qa_highlights.question: LAP profitability, branch breakeven, and LAP ROA/ROE targets?
qa_highlights.answer: LAP breakeven expected around Q3 FY27; branch breakeven takes about 7-8 months versus 16-18 months for an average branch, with over 40% of LAP customers from the PL base. LAP ROE target is 20%+, with no separate ROA figure given.

risks_watch: Revenue margin compression: total income fell 249 bps of average AUM QoQ, with off-book share rising to 53.6%; watch whether PPOP and PAT keep growing as the margin falls.

Industry stress: management flagged bureau-visible stress in small-ticket and multi-lender borrowers and AI-related salaried profile changes; 270 pin codes remain paused and an approval-band change (3.7 vs 4) is under review.

Cost of borrowing: guidance for at least 100 bps reduction over three quarters depends on debt repricing; the Q1 incremental raise was at about 12.9% loaded, and the ratings upgrade from India Ratings/CRISIL is only under discussion and would affect FY28 more than FY27.
Gross NPA rose while credit cost fell; management attributed this to write-off timing (150 DPD) and Stage 2 seasonality. Track Stage 2 (3.15%) and GNPA (2.25%) in Q2.
FLDG accounting: the 5% upfront FLDG is blocked capital, and utilised FLDG sits in credit cost or opex; the Q1 FLDG opex amount was not disclosed (Krishnan estimated about 1%).
LAP breakeven (around Q3 FY27) and the new mutual fund distribution line (AMFI registration only; no size or timing) are still unproven.
key_quotes: Credit cost was 6.80% of average AUM, down from 7.02% in Q4 FY26 and 8.85% in Q1 FY26.
We firmly hold to our guidance which we gave last quarter, which is 15% reduction in credit cost , and we are tracking well on that.
As we said last quarter, we would rather carry prudence slightly early than discover optimism slightly late.
The bureau data tells a two -sided story, while our craft lies in telling the two sides apart.
summary.management_tone: Confident and reassuring on asset quality, credit cost and FY27 guidance, which management reiterated as on track. It was more cautious on the pace of pin-code reopening, the pricing and yield trajectory, and the timing of cost-of-funds benefits, and it declined to give a product-wise NIM or the FLDG opex amount.
